text.p: LONDON, Dec 13 (Reuter ) - The dollar got a late boost in Europe on news the European Union (EU) reached a deal on a post-monetary union stability pact to ensure ensure fiscal discipline in a single currency Europe.

The news knocked the mark lower versus the dollar and its European crosses but dealers noted the impact was limited as agreement on the stability pact had been expected. "It looks as if Germany has climbed down from its tough demands. That should be bad news for the mark and good news for the high-yielders," said Nick Stamenkovic at DKB International.

At 1622 GMT the dollar was at 1.5470/80 marks and 113.95/114.05, up from 1.5445/55 and 113.52/62 in late European trading on Thursday. EU leaders agreed countries should be exempt from fines if GDP contracts two percent, while a 0.75 percent to two percent contraction will result in fines being levied for excessive deficits if agreed by EU governments. Stamenkovic said the deal suggested the German government agreed to a compromise by softening their demands for a tough pact and for automatic sanctions. "This should give a new lease of life to the convergence trades," said Stamenkovic. The agreement is likely to smooth the way towards monetary union and lessen speculative pressures on more vulnerable European currencies. The mark's reaction was more pronounced on its European crosses, with mark/French franc dropping to a near seven-month low of 3.3719 versus 3.3831/38 in late European trading on Thursday. Mark/lira was at 986.70/987.00 from 998.22/989.57. Mark weakness in the wake of the stability pact deal should now help dollar/mark to notch up further gains above 1.55 marks, dealers said. "It's encouraging to see how the dollar held above 1.54 with all the trouble in the U.S. asset markets lately," said Brian Kiely, treasury technician at Royal Bank of Scotland. The dollar firmed against the yen after U.S. names bought the unit in the lower 113 yen region, setting the stage for a test of of 114 yen, traders said. Dealers noted the dollar was also buoyed by unconfirmed rumours circulating that a Washington-based consultancy had issued a report saying that Japanese officials would tolerate a dollar/yen rate of 120 yen. "It helped the general trend higher," said a UK bank trader. The prospect of a soft euro, which has increased after the stability pact compromise deal, will also be a boon for the dollar as investors might chose to switch to dollars at the onset of monetary union, analysts said.

The ailing Swiss franc found some support from comments by Swiss National Bank board member Bruno Gehring who said the franc was no longer clearly overvalued. The SNB said no more official rate cuts were to be expected soon. Dollar/Swiss was at 1.3170/80 from 1.3142/52, while mark/Swiss stood at 85.12 from 85.02/10. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
